text_version.note: AGORA record covers part of an act: JSP 936 V1.1 Dependable Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Defence (part 1: directive)

territorial_scope.description: Applies to MOD staff, MOD AI capabilities and suppliers contracted by MOD; the text does not extend it to non-MOD actors.

evidence.quote: This JSP must be applied by all MOD staff in all phases of the system life cycle

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: UK Ministry of Defence directive (JSP 936 Part 1) setting mandatory requirements for dependable AI in Defence: ethical principles, governance, human-AI teaming, lifecycle controls, safety, security and supplier assurance. Applies to all MOD staff and AI across the system lifecycle; the extract states no commencement date.
summary.long: JSP 936 Part 1 is a UK Ministry of Defence directive on dependable artificial intelligence. It adopts a broad characterisation of AI and covers AI in Robotic and Autonomous Systems and digital systems across all lifecycle phases, from pre-concept to disposal. Tailoring of its requirements is permitted only after a risk assessment. It requires an AI ethical risk assessment at project outset, structured around five MOD ethical principles: human-centricity, responsibility, understanding, bias and harm mitigation, and reliability. Each TLB must appoint a Responsible AI Senior Officer (RAISO) and provide annual Statements of AI Ethical Assurance. Overall risk ratings determine approval levels, and special-attention uses such as AI in kinetic effects are referred to the DAU. Operative requirements cover human-centred design, allocation of functions between humans and AI, data correctness and provenance, model documentation, verification and validation, safety and security analysis, disclosure of AI use in products, and supplier competence. The extract contains no penalties and no commencement date. Its requirements are expressed as 'must' provisions addressed to MOD staff and suppliers, and Part 2 guidance is stated to follow.

events.note: The text gives no adoption, signature, publication, entry-into-force or application date and no phase-in schedule. Para 99 requires TLB Executive Boards to provide Statements of AI Ethical Assurance to 2PUS on an annual basis, a recurring reporting cycle with no stated deadline date or legal consequence, so it is not coded as an event.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changing legal treatment appears in the operative text. Risk-rating tiers (major and above risk, medium or high risk) are categories rather than numbers. Table 1 (ethical risk referral levels) is omitted from the fetched text. The annual Statement of AI Ethical Assurance (para 99) is a reporting frequency, not a threshold.
